info.name: Student ID - Moderation Service
info.description:
Moderation Service (Java), reached through the Gateway on {{baseUrl}} as the communication contract requires: no request here talks to the service's own port. Lab 4: there are no mocks. Decisions are scored from the real Session, Applicant, Credential and Rules owners through the Message Broker (Lab 4: topic publications, over gRPC from Task 8; see docs/messaging-grpc.md), so this collection needs a real session ({{sessionId}}) in which the moderator, junior and outsider tokens hold those roles, and real applicants of that session whose owners generated the stated deceptions ({{applicantBanned}}, {{applicantRuleBreaker}}, {{applicantInconsistent}}, {{applicantExpiredDocument}}). Until every operation marked requested in the catalog is implemented by its owner, submit requests fail closed with 503 <DEPENDENCY>_UNAVAILABLE, which is the expected behaviour, not a pass.

Authentication: every request sends Bearer the appropriate private player token, a real access JWT of that player (Player login, or a disposable local test signer whose public key the Gateway and DMs are configured with). The Gateway verifies it and sets X-Player-Id from its subject, so this collection sends no X-Player-Id: identity cannot be chosen by the client. Keep tokens in a private Postman environment, never in tracked files. The health request uses no authentication. Penalty-policy writes use {{policyAdminToken}}, a player listed in MODERATION_POLICY_ADMINS. Lab 4 folders: Task 3 Gateway boundary, Task 4 operational logs (log-download endpoint), Tasks 5-8 Message Broker (topics, events, topic listing). HTTP topic publication tests exercise the Broker compatibility ingress; native gRPC publication uses messaging.proto. Broker-to-service gRPC delivery requires a matching transport catalog and healthy receivers.

item.name: Lab 4 Task 4 - Operational logs
item.description: Start the local log-download endpoint (scripts/log_download.py) for the exact running Compose project. Set logDownloadUrl and a private logDownloadToken; this is a separate operations credential, not a Player JWT. The download is limited to moderation-service and its declared numeric replicas; omit the service query on the same endpoint for the whole system.

exec: pm.test('Exporter is UP', () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.service).to.eql('log-download-service'); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('UP'); });

request.description: A finite text attachment from the selected Compose project. Use Save Response to keep it privately. A 503 means the local Docker/configuration source is unavailable.

exec: pm.test('Owned service snapshot includes the requested bounds', () => { const text = pm.response.text(); pm.expect(text).to.include('services=moderation-service'); pm.expect(text).to.include('since=15m; tail=200 per container'); });

pm.test('Operations authentication error is traceable', () => { const error = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(error.code).to.eql('UNAUTHORIZED'); pm.expect(error.service).to.eql('log-download-service'); pm.expect(error.traceId).to.eql(pm.response.headers.get('X-Trace-Id')); });
pm.test('Invalid query uses the operations contract', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql('INVALID_LOG_QUERY'));

item.name: Lab 4 Tasks 5-8 - Message Broker
item.description: Service-to-service messaging through the Message Broker (grades 5-8). Run where brokerBaseUrl reaches the Broker on the private network (for example newman inside the Compose network, http://message-broker:8093). The tokens are Broker CALLER credentials of the named services, supplied privately; never commit them. gRPC (Task 8: MessageBroker on :9093, MessageConsumer.Deliver on Moderation's :9080) uses contracts/proto/studentid/messaging/v1/messaging.proto in Postman's gRPC requests, which the v2.1 collection format cannot carry; the HTTP publication API below reaches the same queues, so the Broker delivers to Moderation over gRPC once transports.json names moderation-service grpc.

request.description: Lab 4 Grade 7: GET /internal/v1/messaging/topics with a Broker caller credential. gRPC MessageBroker.ListTopics returns the same listing.

exec: pm.test('Every reviewed topic, sorted', () => { const names = listing.topics.map(t => t.topic); pm.expect(names.length).to.eql(44); pm.expect(names).to.eql([...names].sort()); });

pm.test('operation.moderation.applicantDecisionFacts.v1 has a ready moderation-service subscriber', () => { const t = listing.topics.find(x => x.topic === 'operation.moderation.applicantDecisionFacts.v1'); pm.expect(t).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(listing.discovery).to.eql('UP'); pm.expect(t.subscribers['moderation-service'].ready).to.be.above(0); });

item.name: Rules asks Moderation for decision facts (topic publication)

request.description: Grade 6: a request topic. The Broker (grade 5) picks a ready Moderation replica by round robin behind its circuit breaker and returns Moderation's exact status and body.

exec: // The Task 6 envelope: fresh transport ids, a UTC deadline the broker caps to its budget.
return JSON.stringify({messageId: pm.variables.get('messageId'), schemaVersion: 1, kind: kind, topic: topic,
function group(name) { const g = pm.response.json().groups[name]; return Object.assign({}, g, {body: g.bodyBase64 ? JSON.parse(atob(g.bodyBase64)) : null}); }

pm.test('Moderation answered with its facts', () => { const g = group('moderation-service'); pm.expect(g.acknowledged).to.eql(true); pm.expect(g.status).to.eql(200); pm.expect(g.body.applicantId).to.eql(pm.variables.get('applicantBanned')); pm.expect(g.body.previouslyBanned).to.be.a('boolean'); });
